major_concerns: Verifier coverage vs real devices (false negatives/positives) may bias measured improvements.
Risk of overfitting generated repairs to verifier semantics while leaving unmodeled side-effects.
Task selection/exclusion (vendor-CLI) could limit external validity.
Prompt sanitation and injection vectors not fully specified; security risk.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register a diverse task set and inclusion/exclusion rules that justify digital-twin choices and document limitations.
Use multiple verifier configurations or cross-validate with a second verifier to reduce single-verifier bias.
Add measurements for unmodeled side-effects (e.g., simulated side-channel checks) and report them.
Specify exact prompt templates, seeds, model identifier, and repair prompt policy in preregistration; include prompt-sanitization steps.

major_concerns: Many provider APIs do not expose reliable token/sequence log-probabilities; primary predictors may be unavailable.
Calibration may not generalize across prompt templates, model versions, or OOD/adversarial intents.
Operational thresholds could induce impractically high false-block rates.
Dataset representativeness and label balance may affect AUROC/AUPRC estimates.
required_design_repairs: Specify fallback confidence signals if log-probs are unavailable (e.g., n-best sampling diversity, model self-evaluation prompts) and preregister which will be primary.
Pre-register calibration fold split, transfer/generalization tests (different prompts and model versions), and adversarial/OOD evaluation.
Conduct and report a power/sample-size analysis for detecting expected AUROC improvements; predefine operational thresholds and utility metrics.
Log and report API limitations (missing logprobs) and how that affected reproducibility.

major_concerns: Constructed attack benchmark may not reflect real adversary creativity (external validity).
Ethical risk: publishing concrete injection payloads could aid adversaries.
Grammar-constrained decoding may produce high rejection or break legitimate constructs, biasing results.
Tuning metadata-gating rules could be subjective and alter measured effectiveness.
required_design_repairs: Define and disclose a clear threat model and benchmark curation policy; restrict public release of attack payloads or sanitize them to mitigate dual-use risk.
Pre-register diverse attack classes, source them from literature where possible, and include held-out real-world-like variants to test generalization.
Measure utility impact (rejection and inability-to-produce rates) and include these in main outcomes.
Specify deterministic, auditable metadata-gating rules and grammar-constraint implementations; report tuning steps and avoid post-hoc adjustments.

major_concerns: Marginal-return patterns may be highly task- and verifier-dependent, limiting generality.
Regressions (pass→fail) could be rare and require large samples to quantify reliably.
Cost-effectiveness metric depends on provider pricing and assumed operational costs; sensitivity analysis needed.
Stopping-rule threshold choice may be arbitrary without power/sample-size justification.
required_design_repairs: Include a preregistered power/sample-size calculation to detect expected marginal improvements and regression rates.
Predefine and justify the marginal-improvement stopping threshold and perform sensitivity analyses over thresholds.
Use a diverse task set and, if possible, multiple verifier configurations to assess generality.
Report cost-effectiveness under multiple pricing/call-cost assumptions and include bootstrap uncertainty for cost metrics.
